activity.justification: MIC <= 32 ug/ml is the common antibacterial-activity convention named as the candidate breakpoint in plan.md phase 1. Verified against the data on 28 Aug 2026: yields 51-74% active across the five priority species (E. coli 62.4%, S. aureus 62.3%, P. aeruginosa 60.5%, K. pneumoniae 51.4%, A. baumannii 73.9%), all inside the 85/15 class-balance gate. A 16 ug/ml cut was also measured (~50/50) and kept as a sensitivity option.
activity.collapse_rule: majority vote over a sequence's measurements, ties active
activity.censoring_rule: right-censored '>X' with X >= threshold is a definitive INACTIVE and is kept; with X < threshold it is ambiguous and dropped. Never discard censored rows wholesale - they carry the negative class.

toxicity.justification: The lysis table stores (effect level, dose that produced it), NOT (dose, percent). So the label is dose-anchored: toxic = reaches >=50% hemolysis of human erythrocytes at a dose <= 100 ug/ml; safe = tested at >= 100 ug/ml without ever reaching 50%; everything else is unlabeled and dropped. The 100 ug/ml reference matches the dataset's own Notes convention ('Not active up to 100 micro g/ml'). Verified 28 Aug 2026: 270 labeled sequences, 36.3% toxic.
